items.title: Readiness scores used as a gate without predictive evidence
items.whyItMatters: Prediction was tested for few tools and not found in the one prospective study (claims c1, c2).
items.opportunity: Frame readiness assessment as planning and conversation, and state the absence of predictive evidence plainly.

items.title: Scores track literacy and deprivation
items.whyItMatters: A threshold would delay transfer for disadvantaged young people (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Review adapted, supported and translated approaches.

items.title: Ceiling effects after 16
items.whyItMatters: The questionnaire cannot distinguish older adolescents, exactly when transfer is decided.
items.opportunity: Summarise evidence on item range and condition-neutral wording.

items.title: Young people with learning disabilities
items.whyItMatters: Standard tools cannot be completed independently.
items.opportunity: Include adapted tools and carer perspectives.

errorsFound: The first scan reply was markdown with a table of evidence strengths, not the structured appraisal; nothing from it was applied.
reevaluation: The narrative review should examine what readiness means to young people, what tools measure, the weak evidence for prediction, and fair alternatives for disadvantaged groups.
summary: Four gaps; gatekeeping without predictive evidence and inequity are high severity.
